When ego replaces trust, courts can't save a marriage, Madras HC

The Madras High Court has upheld a Family Court decree granting divorce to a husband, holding that courts cannot preserve a marriage once mutual trust has irretrievably broken down and the relationship has become emotionally unworkable.

The case arose from a marriage solemnised in 2015, from which a daughter was born. The husband sought divorce alleging repeated matrimonial disputes, while the wife later filed a petition seeking restitution of conjugal rights to resume married life.

After examining the evidence, the High Court found that the parties' relationship had deteriorated beyond repair and that legal intervention could not restore a marriage where trust and mutual respect had ceased to exist.

The Court observed that a successful marriage rests on mutual respect, tolerance and placing the welfare of the family above individual ego. It remarked that when ego replaces empathy, disagreements escalate into prolonged conflict and the law becomes powerless to save the relationship.

While affirming the decree of divorce, the Bench also referred to the importance of resolving misunderstandings with humility rather than allowing pride to destroy matrimonial relationships.

The High Court clarified that the divorce decree would not affect the wife's existing maintenance rights and directed the husband to continue complying with all maintenance orders passed by the competent courts.
